facts.text: Lambton County, home to Sarnia, is the birthplace of North America's oil industry and today is Canada's second largest petrochemical cluster.
facts.evidence: Lambton County is the birthplace of North America's oil industry (1858) and today is Canada's 2nd largest petrochemical cluster.

facts.text: Bluewater Health is a major public employer in Sarnia with 1,700 employees.
facts.evidence: Other significant employers include public sector organizations like Bluewater Health (1,700 employees) and the Lambton Kent District School Board (1,150 employees).

facts.text: Major private employers in Sarnia-Lambton include NOVA Chemicals with 943 employees and Imperial's Sarnia Manufacturing Site with 870 employees.
facts.evidence: Major private employers include NOVA Chemicals (Canada) Ltd. with 943 current employees and Imperial's Sarnia Manufacturing Site with 870 current employees.

facts.text: Sarnia-Lambton's economic partnership works with businesses in agri-food processing, chemicals and energy, hydrogen, advanced manufacturing, and EV and battery supply chains.
facts.evidence: The Sarnia-Lambton Economic Partnership works with existing businesses in the value-added agricultural & food processing, chemicals & energy, hydrogen, advanced manufacturing, and EV & battery supply chain sectors.

facts.text: Lambton College's Sarnia campus has about 30 per cent fewer students after changes to international student visa programs.
facts.evidence: There are about 30 per cent fewer students at the Sarnia campus this year due to changes to the International Student Visa programs.

meta.descriptor: the largest city on Lake Huron, in Lambton County
meta.fact: the centre of Canada's Chemical Valley, with NOVA Chemicals and Imperial among its largest employers

overview: Sarnia had 72,047 residents in 2021, a 0.6 per cent rise from 2016, in 32,188 occupied homes. With a near-flat population, growth for a local business comes from winning customers away from competitors rather than from a wave of newcomers.

The economy rests on petrochemical plants, Bluewater Health and Lambton College, alongside newer work in hydrogen and battery supply chains. Industrial employers and their contractors form a valuable business-to-business market, while household spending supports retail and services across the city.

byService.lead-generation: Because Sarnia grew only 0.6 per cent between 2016 and 2021, lead generation should focus on converting existing households and the contractors who supply the city's petrochemical plants.
byService.seo: In a stable market of about 72,000 people, Sarnia SEO wins by out-ranking established competitors on specific services and neighbourhood terms such as Brights Grove and downtown.
byService.website-development: Sarnia firms selling to industrial clients need websites that show safety credentials, certifications and project experience clearly, since plant buyers check those details before calling.
byService.branding: Loyalty runs deep in a long-settled city like Sarnia, so branding should stress reliability and local history to pull customers from businesses they have used for years.
